The first pre-release of v5, the fork's next major version. It rebuilds the components on one foundation, and lets you write and share your own the same way. It's on npm under the `next-experimental` tag, so an install without a version still gets 4.x. Built on sst-community [v4.20.0](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/releases/tag/v4.20.0) with the fixes on `main` since, and on upstream [v4.17.2](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/releases/tag/v4.17.2).

It's a build to try v5 with, on a stage of its own. The v5 components can still change in any way before 5.0.0. The 4.x components in `sst.aws.*` work as they do in 4.x, so an app can move to this CLI first and switch its components one at a time.

### ⚠️ Breaking changes

- **A `version` rule in `sst.config.ts` has to name a pre-release to accept this one.** `">= 5.0.0-0"` accepts `5.0.0-alpha.1`, but `">= 4"`, `"5.x"` and `"*"` don't. Change the rule or remove it before you install.
- **A provider version in your config has to be in the major version SST's components are built for**, or before 1.0, the minor version. An older one was already refused, and now a newer one is too, with the versions to use. `sst add` picks the newest version in that major version instead of npm's `latest`.
- **Deployed function roles no longer trust the account root**, only Lambda. `sst dev` still adds it. The first deploy updates every function's role in place, so a deploy role with limited permissions needs `iam:UpdateAssumeRolePolicy`. Add it before you update. ([#95](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/95), [anomalyco/sst#7026](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/issues/7026))

### New

- **v5 components, next to the 4.x ones.** 20 are ported, as `sst.aws.v5.*`: `Alb`, `ApiGatewayV2`, `AppSync`, `Aurora`, `Bucket`, `Bus`, `Cluster`, `CognitoUserPool`, `CronV2`, `Dsql`, `Dynamo`, `Efs`, `Function`, `Mysql`, `Postgres`, `Queue`, `Redis`, `Service`, `SnsTopic` and `Task`. Each declares every resource it creates as a part, and from that list gives you `transform` for any of them, `existing` to use one you already have, and `nodes` to read any of them. See the [README](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/tree/v5.0.0-alpha.1#readme).
- **Switch one component at a time and keep what's deployed.** Change `sst.aws.Queue` to `sst.aws.v5.Queue`, keep the name, and the resources stay. An object `transform` is merged deeply in v5, where 4.x replaced what it named. Each component's doc comment, in [`platform/src/components/aws/v5/`](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/tree/v5.0.0-alpha.1/platform/src/components/aws/v5), has a "Switch from" section with what else is written differently.
- **Write your own components** with `sst.component()`, the way SST's own are made, from resources of any provider in your app. Whoever uses one gets `transform`, `existing` and `nodes` for each of its parts, and a `link()` method makes it linkable. See [Write a Local Component](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/blob/v5.0.0-alpha.1/www/src/content/docs/docs/write-a-local-component.mdx).
- **Share components as npm packages.** A package imports `sst/components` and its providers and lists them as peer dependencies. When an app deploys it, the package gets the app's copies. The deploy checks those peer dependencies, and says to run `sst add` for a missing provider. An app without a `package.json` lists packages in its config, under `packages`. See [Write a Package Component](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/blob/v5.0.0-alpha.1/www/src/content/docs/docs/write-a-package-component.mdx).
- **Test components without AWS.** `mock()` stands in for the deploy engine, so a test creates a component and checks what it would deploy. A package's repo imports it from `sst/testing`.
- **`sst install` writes `.sst/tsconfig.json`**, which says where the app's SST and providers are. An app's `tsconfig.json` extends it, so TypeScript reads a package's types.
- **`sst upgrade` and `sst init` stay in the CLI's major version.** This CLI upgrades to the newest 5.x, pre-releases included.
- **"X is not defined" in a config says how to add the provider**, with `sst add`.
- **`sst.aws.Redis` can create an ElastiCache Serverless cache**, with [`serverless`](https://sst-community.github.io/sst/docs/component/aws/redis#serverless). ([#91](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/91), [anomalyco/sst#6160](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/issues/6160))

### Fixes

- **`sst dev` sends a function's response again when it doesn't arrive.** Right after a function cold-starts, AppSync can take a response and not deliver it, and the call hung until it timed out. The CLI now sends each response and error five times, three seconds apart, and the function keeps the first to arrive. ([#102](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/102), [anomalyco/sst#6575](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/issues/6575))
- **Functions on a shared `bundle` each read their own linked resources.** They shared one file, so the last one written won, and every deploy uploaded their code again. ([#89](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/89), [anomalyco/sst#6750](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/pull/6750))
- **`sst dev`'s memory stops growing as functions rebuild.** It keeps at most 4 esbuild build contexts. `SST_BUILD_CONTEXT_CACHE` sets the number, and `0` turns the cache off. ([#90](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/90), [anomalyco/sst#6960](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/pull/6960))
- **A rebuild in `sst dev` no longer deletes a function's output from under a running worker**, which broke functions with several bridge instances, such as behind CloudFront or a `Router`. ([#100](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/100), [anomalyco/sst#6416](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/issues/6416))

### Known issues

- **Not ported yet:** the sites (`Nextjs`, `Astro`, `StaticSite` and the rest), `Vpc`, `Router`, `Cdn`, `MicroVm`, the Cloudflare and Vercel components, and others. They work as 4.x components. The [plan](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/blob/v5.0.0-alpha.1/docs/plans/v5-components.md#status) lists them.
- **`sst diff` can show a function as deleted that the deploy then updates**, when its args hold a value that isn't known until the deploy. 4.x does the same.
- **Not tried in AWS yet:** `sst dev` with a v5 `Service` or `Task`, `get` and `existing` with real resources, and a custom `provider`.
- **`Mysql` without a `version` can't be created**, as RDS no longer offers its default, 8.0.40. 4.x has the same problem. Set a `version`.

### Install

```bash
npm install sst@npm:@sst-community/sst@5.0.0-alpha.1
```

To try it in an existing project:

1. Use a stage of its own, and check that `version` in `sst.config.ts` accepts a pre-release.
2. Set its dependency to `"sst": "npm:@sst-community/sst@5.0.0-alpha.1"` and reinstall.
3. To go back, set it to `4.20.0` again. Switch any v5 components back to their 4.x names first.

For a project that isn't JavaScript, install the CLI globally. This replaces a global 4.x CLI:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sst-community/sst/main/install | VERSION=5.0.0-alpha.1 bash
```
